grammar.title: Precision: choosing the word that fits
grammar.intro: At C1 the grammar is largely settled; what separates you from a native is lexical precision. Spanish splits meanings English merges (saber vs conocer, pedir vs preguntar), fixes certain noun+verb collocations (you tomas a decision, you don't 'haces' it), and hides false friends (actual means current, not actual). This unit trains you to pick the word context and register actually demand.

sections.heading: Near-synonyms English merges
sections.body: These pairs collapse into one English verb but stay distinct in Spanish. Master the boundary: saber a fact/skill vs conocer a person/place; pedir = request a thing vs preguntar = ask a question; llevar (take away from here) vs traer (bring towards here):
conj: to know a fact / how to

ex.es: Conozco Madrid, pero no sé llegar a tu barrio.
ex.en: I know Madrid, but I don't know how to get to your neighbourhood.
ex.note: conocer un lugar · saber + infinitivo (a skill)

ex.es: Me preguntó la hora y luego me pidió un favor.
ex.en: She asked me the time and then asked me for a favour.
ex.note: preguntar = pose a question · pedir = request something

sections.heading: Collocations: the verb the noun expects
sections.body: Natives pair certain nouns with a fixed verb. Translating word-for-word from English produces odd Spanish. You tomas a decision (not 'haces'), cometes a mistake (not 'haces'), and prestas attention (not 'pagas'). Also weigh hacer (to do/make, general) vs realizar (to carry out, formal):

ex.es: Antes de tomar una decisión, presta atención a los detalles.
ex.en: Before making a decision, pay attention to the details.
ex.note: tomar una decisión · prestar atención (fixed pairings)

ex.es: El equipo realizó un estudio riguroso y no cometió ni un error.
ex.en: The team carried out a rigorous study and didn't make a single mistake.

sections.heading: False friends that trip up C1 speakers
sections.body: These look English but mean something else. Using them literally is a classic advanced slip. Learn the real Spanish meaning — and the word English speakers really wanted:

ex.es: En la situación actual, asistí a la reunión aunque estaba constipado.
ex.en: In the current situation, I attended the meeting even though I had a cold.
ex.note: actual = current · asistir a = attend · constipado = with a cold

ex.es: Es una persona muy sensible; el éxito no le ha cambiado.
ex.en: She's a very sensitive person; success hasn't changed her.

takeaways: saber a fact/skill vs conocer a person/place; pedir = request vs preguntar = ask a question.
Collocations are fixed: tomar una decisión, cometer un error, prestar atención, hacer caso.
hacer = do/make (general); realizar = carry out (formal register).
False friends: actual = current, asistir = attend, éxito = success, sensible = sensitive, constipado = with a cold.

mistakes.why: The collocation is tomar una decisión, not 'hacer una decisión' (an anglicism).

mistakes.w: Le pregunté un vaso de agua.
mistakes.r: Le pedí un vaso de agua.
mistakes.why: Requesting a thing is pedir; preguntar is only for asking questions.

mistakes.w: Estoy muy embarazada por lo que dije.
mistakes.r: Estoy muy avergonzada por lo que dije.
mistakes.why: embarazada means pregnant; ‘embarrassed’ is avergonzada — a classic false friend.

exercises.prompt: No ___ a nadie en esta ciudad todavía.
exercises.prompt_en: I don't know anyone in this city yet.
exercises.no: Being acquainted with people uses conocer, not saber: “No conozco a nadie…”.

exercises.prompt: Antes de invertir, conviene ___ una decisión meditada.
exercises.prompt_en: Before investing, it's advisable to make a considered decision.
exercises.no: The fixed collocation is tomar una decisión — ‘hacer una decisión’ is an anglicism.

exercises.prompt: Build: “She attended the meeting even though she had a cold.”
exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! asistir a = attend · constipada = with a cold.
exercises.no: “Asistió a la reunión aunque estaba constipada” — asistir a = attend, constipada = with a cold (not embarazada).

exercises.prompt: El camarero se acercó y le ___ la cuenta.
exercises.prompt_en: The waiter came over and asked him for the bill.
exercises.hint: To request a thing (not to pose a question).
exercises.no: Requesting a thing → pedir: “le pidió la cuenta”. (preguntar is only for questions.)

exercises.prompt: Match each false friend to its true Spanish meaning.

exercises.tts: Presta atención a lo que voy a decirte.
accepted: presta atencion a lo que voy a decirte
exercises.translation: Pay attention to what I'm going to tell you.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Presta atención a lo que voy a decirte.”
exercises.no: It was: “Presta atención a lo que voy a decirte.” (prestar atención = to pay attention)

exercises.scenario: A friend praises how well your new venture is going 🚀

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.es: He oído que tu proyecto va viento en popa. ¡Enhorabuena!
lines.en: I've heard your project is going great. Congratulations!

options.text: Gracias, la verdad es que ha sido todo un éxito.
Gracias, la verdad es que ha sido toda una salida.
Gracias, la verdad es que estoy muy embarazado.

exercises.no: ‘Success’ is éxito (not salida = exit, nor embarazado = pregnant).

exercises.say: No sé conducir, pero conozco la ruta.
exercises.en: I don't know how to drive, but I know the route.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “No sé conducir, pero conozco la ruta.”
